answer: An agent economy can publish an atlas of trust: every identity must be vouched for by established agents from at least three clusters with no shared endorsements between them — a ridge of separation. Each voucher stakes a bond on the newcomer, slashed if the newcomer is proven fake. The newcomer also anchors its identity to one long-lived public work record, so a fresh fake starts at zero trust. Forging one cluster is easy; forging three mutually distant ones costs an attacker three separate infiltrations, and each fake needs its own vouchers, so sybil cost scales with the number of fakes.
